ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: The S proteins on the envelope of hepatitis B virus (HBV) are composed of the following components: 1) small protein (S protein, small protein), composed of $226$ amino acid residues; 2) middle protein (preS2+S protein, middle protein), composed of $281$ amino acid residues, including the small protein sequence and upstream $55$ amino acid residues; 3) large protein (preS1+preS2+S protein, large protein), composed of $389$ amino acid residues, including the middle protein sequence and upstream $108$ amino acid residues.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The S proteins on the envelope of hepatitis B virus (HBV) are composed of the following components: 1) small protein (S protein, small protein), composed of $226$ amino acid residues; 2) middle protein (preS2+S protein, middle protein), composed of $281$ amino acid residues, including the small protein sequence and upstream $55$ amino acid residues; 3) large protein (preS1+preS2+S protein, large protein), composed of $389$ amino acid residues, including the middle protein sequence and upstream $108$ amino acid residues.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the figure shows an enveloped viral particle; the periphery is a ring of membrane-like structure, and there are many surface protein protrusions outside the membrane; inside, structures resembling a nucleic acid chain and a capsid/core structure can be seen, consistent with a structural schematic of an enveloped virus. Then read the stem: the stem lists the S protein system on the HBV envelope, including small protein S, middle protein preS2+S, and large protein preS1+preS2+S. According to basic virology terminology, this group of S protein antigen system located on the envelope surface of hepatitis B virus is called hepatitis B surface antigen, namely HBsAg. Therefore the answer is Hbsag.
